The Cardinals have until Nov. 4 to return the 24-year-old to the active roster, or he will be forced to spend the remainder of the 2026 season on injured reserve.

headline: The Cardinals placed Crawford (ankle) on their injured reserve list Wednesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Crawford sustained a mid ankle sprain and was carted off the field during the second half of Sunday's win against the Chargers, and now he'll have to sit out at least Arizona's next four games. Until he's able to return to action, 2024 fourth-rounder Dadrion Taylor-Demerson (ribs) and undrafted rookie Wydett Williams could be in line for a slight increase in reps.

headline: Crawford (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Chargers, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Crawford appeared to suffer the injury on a punt play in the second half. He was carted off the sidelines to the locker room, where he is undergoing further tests to determine the severity of the injury. Crawford logged three tackles (two solo), prior to his exit, and Wydett Williams will be the lone backup safety if Crawford doesn't return.

headline: Collins (hip) is active for Sunday's game against the Rams.
story: Collins sustained a hip injury during Friday's practice and was unable to participate in the session. Despite the new injury, the starting strongside linebacker is all set to suit up for Sunday's divisional contest against the Rams.

headline: Collins (hip) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Rams, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
story: Collins showed up on Friday's injury report with a new hip injury and was unable to practice. The Cardinals' starting strongside linebacker will likely miss Sunday's game due to the issue, leaving Baron Browning to start against the Rams.

headline: Terrell (back) is now recovering from an illness ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Terrell is still listed as questionable, but he now has to overcome an illness as well as a back injury in order to be available for Sunday's home contest. His potential absence would mean less depth in the secondary for the Falcons, although the team got reinforcements thanks to the activation of A.J. Terrell (groin) from injured reserve.

headline: Terrell (head) returned to Sunday's game against the Bears, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Terrell exited the contest to be evaluated for a right-side stinger and concussion. However, the rookie was cleared by team medical staff and returned to the game.

headline: Terrell (head) is questionable to return to Sunday's game versus Chicago, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Terrell not only suffered a right-side stinger but is also being evaluated for a concussion. With A.J. Terrell (groin) on injured reserve and C.J. Henderson (groin) ruled out, Mike Ford should see more snaps alongside Mike Hughes.

headline: The Falcons placed Jerrell (biceps) on injured reserve Saturday, Tori McElhaney of the team's official site reports.
story: Jerrell was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the 49ers due to a biceps injury. He's now required to miss at least four games, so the next time he's eligible to play is Week 12 against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29. Jerrell's absence leaves the Falcons with less depth on the offensive line.

headline: Jerrell (biceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Jerrell didn't practice Thursday or Friday due to a biceps injury, which is severe enough for him to miss Sunday's game. The Falcons will have less depth on the offensive line because of the absence of Jerrell, whose next chance to play is Week 8 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: The Falcons elevated Herbert from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Tori McElhaney of the team's official site reports.
story: Herbert is set to suit up for his 2026 regular-season debut as the No. 2 running back behind Bijan Robinson for Sunday's game against the 49ers. The 28-year-old will take relief snaps in place of Brian Robinson (hamstring), who has been ruled out due to injury.

headline: After Brian Robinson (hamstring) was ruled out, Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said Friday that Herbert will be Bijan Robinson's backup against the 49ers on Sunday, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Herbert has been on the practice squad for the past month but will be elevated for RB2 duties against San Francisco. He carried the ball 16 times for 52 yards (3.3 YPC) across seven appearances with the Jets last season but hasn't been a productive rusher since 2023 with the Bears.

headline: The Falcons signed Herbert to the practice squad Wednesday, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Herbert entered the league in 2021 and has suited up for the Bears, Bengals and Jets. In 63 regular-season games, the 28-year-old amassed 1,957 yards and nine touchdowns off 416 carries, adding 54 catches for 316 yards and two touchdowns. While the Falcons have Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson in the backfield, Herbert could be elevated if one of those players gets hurt down the line.

headline: Collins (hip) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Collins was looking to make his 2026 debut in Week 7 but has not recovered enough from his hip injury to suit up. The wide receiver must be activated from IR by Nov. 12, or he will spend the entirety of the 2026 season confined to the list.

headline: Collins (hip) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Collins opened the season on injured reserve due to a hip injury, but he was designated to return from IR on Wednesday and strung together an LP-FP-FP practice log during Week 7 prep. He would need to be activated from IR by 4:00 p.m. ET on Saturday in order to be available for Sunday's contest. If he's cleared to play, then most of Collins' work would likely come on special teams, though he would be in the mix for some snaps on offense if Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder) is not cleared to play against San Francisco.

headline: The Falcons designated Collins (hip) to return from IR on Thursday, per the NFL's transaction log.
story: Collins was a limited participant in practice Wednesday. The 23-year-old will likely need to stay on track or upgrade to full participation by Friday for a chance to make his season debut in Week 7.

headline: The Falcons placed Collins (undisclosed) on injured reserve Sunday with a designation to return during the season, Will McFadden of the team's official site reports.
story: Collins did not play in the Falcons' preseason finale against the Dolphins on Friday due to an unknown injury. The wide receiver will now need to miss at least the first four weeks of the regular season before he is permitted to rejoin the team's active roster.

headline: The Falcons activated Terrell (groin) off injured reserve Saturday, Tori McElhaney of the team's official site reports.
story: Terrell has returned to the active roster with no injury designation just in time for the Falcons' game against the 49ers on Sunday. The starting cornerback is all set to suit up opposite Mike Hughes for his first game since Week 2.

headline: Terrell (groin) is questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Terrell was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday and logged a trio of limited practices. He's in the final stages of his recovery from a groin injury that landed him on IR in late September, and Terrell would likely start opposite Mike Hughes at outside cornerback if he's cleared to return Sunday.

headline: Terrell (groin) was a limited participant at the Falcons' practice Wednesday, Daniel Flick of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
story: Terrell had his 21-day practice window opened by Atlanta on Wednesday, and he was able to log a limited session. The cornerback will have two more chances to log a full practice and officially move past the groin injury that has caused him to miss the last four games while on injured reserve.

headline: Terrell (groin) was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official website reports.
story: Terrell has been on injured reserve since Sept. 22 while recovering from a groin injury that he suffered in Week 2 versus the Panthers. The Falcons have now opened the cornerback's 21-day practice window, and if he is not activated before the end of that period, he will remain on IR for the rest of the season.

headline: The Falcons placed Terrell (groin) on injured reserve Tuesday, Tori McElhaney of the team's official site reports.
story: Terrell will be sidelined for at least the Falcons' next four games after sustaining a groin injury in the first quarter of Sunday's 34-3 loss to the Panthers. In Week 2, C.J. Henderson ended up filling in for Terrell at the boundary corner spot opposite Mike Hughes and appears primed to make regular starts so long as Terrell is out of action. The 27-year-old Terrell totaled six tackles and two pass breakups through the Falcons' first two contests of 2026.

headline: Terrell (groin) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Terrell was listed as doubtful to return to Sunday's contest after sustaining a groin injury in the first half. The cornerback avoided a concussion, but the groin issue has stuck enough to rule him out for the remainder of the game. C.J. Henderson is set to play outside cornerback for the Falcons secondary in Terrell's absence.

headline: Terrell is doubtful to return to Sunday's game against the Panthers due to a groin injury, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Terrell was cleared for a concussion, but he was also diagnosed with a groin injury that will likely sideline him for the rest of Sunday's contest. C.J. Henderson will take over at outside corner in Terrell's absence.

headline: Terrell (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: Terrell saw his practice reps limited by a shoulder issue this past week, but he showed enough during pregame warmups to be given the green light to play in Sunday's NFC South showdown. The veteran defensive back logged five tackles (two solo) and one pass defense during the Falcons' 20-13 Week 1 loss to the Steelers.

headline: Terrell (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game versus Carolina.
story: Terrell didn't practice Wednesday but logged a full session Thursday. However, he was absent again Friday, resulting in a questionable designation. With Billy Bowman (Achilles) already ruled out, Avieon Terrell and C.J. Henderson may be tasked with taking on more prominent roles alongside Mike Hughes.

headline: Terrell (shoulder) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: The cornerback told reporters that he would be available to play Sunday against the Panthers, per D. Orlando Ledbetter of BowTieSports.com. Terrell missed practice Wednesday after briefly exiting last Sunday's loss to Pittsburgh following a shoulder injury. He did return to the game and play on 62 defensive snaps overall.

headline: Terrell (shoulder) did not participate at practice Wednesday, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Terrell was able to return to Sunday's loss at Pittsburgh after hurting his shoulder while defending a pass, so Atlanta may just be exercising an abundance of caution. He could still avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend if he practices in full Thursday or Friday.

headline: Bowman (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Bowman was removed from the Falcons' Week 6 loss against the Bears and did not return due to a hamstring injury, which also prevented him from practicing during Week 7 prep. His absence means Sydney Brown should see an uptick in defensive snaps during Sunday's contest, and Bowman's next chance to play is Week 8 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Bowman (hamstring) is doubtful to return to Sunday's game against Atlanta, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Bowman suffered a hamstring injury in the second half of Sunday's contest and is not expected to return. If Bowman can't get back on the field in Week 6, Dee Alford should fill most of the void the rest of the way.

headline: Bowman (Achilles) is available for Thursday's game versus the Packers.
story: Bowman sustained a season-ending Achilles injury ahead of the Week 12 meeting with the Saints during the 2025 campaign. It's unknown if the 23-year-old will be eased back into action. However, Bowman's return, even if it's in a limited capacity, couldn't come at a better time, considering A.J. Terrell (groin) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday. Bowman, No. 118 overall pick in the 2025 Draft, finished his inaugural NFL year with 26 total tackles (15 solo), including 1.5 sacks, one interception and one pass defended in six regular-season games.

headline: Bowman (Achilles) is officially listed as questionable for Thursday's game at Green Bay, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Atlanta only held a walkthrough practice Wednesday, but Bowman was estimated as a full participant, so it seems he's trending in a positive direction ahead of Thursday's contest. If he's not able to make his 2026 debut in Week 3, however, rookie second-rounder Avieon Terrell could continue to see an expanded role in the secondary.

headline: Bowman (Achilles) is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: Despite logging a full practice Friday, Bowman won't suit up for the Week 2 meeting with Carolina. With A.J. Terrell (shoulder) questionable, Atlanta may need to lean more on Avieon Terrell and C.J. Henderson.

headline: Bowman (Achilles) was a limited participant in practice Thursday after participating in full a day earlier, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Bowman passed a physical at the end of training camp, got taken off the active/PUP list and logged limited practices ahead of Week 1, but he still had to sit out of Atlanta's loss to Pittsburgh. The starting slot corner's limited participation Thursday might just be a precaution ahead of Sunday's matchup with Carolina, but if he has to miss the game, Sydney Brown should be in line to step forward in his place.

headline: Bowman (Achilles) was a full participant at practice Wednesday, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Bowman sat out Week 1, as he was still recovering from the Achilles tear he suffered in November of last year, but it looks like he should end up being available in Week 2. He figures to play a major role in Atlanta's secondary in 2026.

headline: Bowman (Achilles) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Steelers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Bowman is still being limited in practice as he recovers from the Achilles tear he sustained in November. The safety is not quite ready to get back on the field, but if he keeps stringing together practices, he may be able to suit up for the Falcons' Week 2 showdown with the Panthers.

headline: Bowman (Achilles) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Bowman was removed from the active/PUP list at the end of training camp after clearing his physical, but his workload is still being limited as he continues to recover from a torn Achilles that he sustained in November. Per Josh Kendall of The Athletic, Bowman said Wednesday that he feels ready to play in Sunday's season opener versus the Steelers, but he was non-committal about suiting up Week 1. His practice participation over the next two days will likely help the Falcons determine his status.

headline: Bowman (Achilles) passed his physical and was activated from the PUP list Sunday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: Bowman continues to make strides in his return from an Achilles injury, and the passed physical marks another positive milestone. Had he landed on the PUP list to open the season, Bowman would have been out for the first four games at minimum. Now it appears the Falcons are confident that they'll have Bowman back in the fold sooner rather than later, even if his status for Week 1 remains murky.

headline: Smith (neck) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Smith opened the week with back-to-back limited practices before logging a full session Friday. He's working through a neck injury that forced him to be sidelined for Week 6 against the Bears, and his status for Sunday's contest may not be officially known until the Falcons announce their list of inactive players about 90 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. Smith's return would bolster the Falcons' depth at the edge rusher position behind Samson Ebukam (hamstring) and Cameron Thomas.

headline: Smith (neck) is active for Sunday's game against the Bears.
story: Smith was limited in Friday's practice with a neck injury after clearing concussion protocol Thursday. The outside linebacker seems to have recovered in time for Sunday's contest and is all set to suit up on the edge against the Bears.

headline: Smith (neck) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bears, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Smith cleared concussion protocol Thursday, but his practice reps have been limited by a neck issue. The veteran pass rusher will continue to get treatment over the weekend, but if he's not cleared to play Sunday, then Jared Ivey would be the lone rotational option behind starters Samson Ebukam and Cameron Thomas.

headline: Smith (neck) was a limited participant at practice Thursday, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Smith's status on Atlanta's official injury report changed from "concussion/neck" to just "neck" Thursday, signaling he has cleared league concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's game versus the Bears. With that said, his availability for Week 6 is still up in the air due to the neck issue, and he may have to log a full practice Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Smith (concussion/neck) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Smith entered the league's concussion protocol during the Falcons' Week 4 win over the Saints on Monday. He drew the questionable tag after practicing in a limited capacity Friday, but it looks like he won't clear protocol before Sunday's game. Samson Ebukam (hamstring) is also listed as questionable, so Jared Ivey, Bralen Trice and Cameron Thomas are all in line for more defensive snaps against Baltimore. Smith's next chance to play is Week 6 against the Bears on Sunday, Oct. 18.

headline: Smith (concussion/neck) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site  reports.
story: Smith was a limited participant in Friday's practice as he continues to deal with a concussion he suffered in the Falcons' win over the Saints on Monday. The linebacker still needs to be cleared for full contact by an independent neurologist. If the 34-year-old still has concussion symptoms Saturday, he will not be able to suit up for Sunday's game.

headline: Smith (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Monday night's game against the Saints, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Smith exited the contest in the first quarter after being down on the field for several minutes. An independent neurologist ruled that the outside linebacker had sustained a concussion, and he will not be allowed to return to the game. Smith will now enter the league's five-step protocol, and his status for a Week 5 matchup against the Ravens on Sunday night will remain in question for the time being.

headline: Smith (neck) is being evaluated for a possible concussion and is questionable to return to Monday's game against the Saints, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Smith took a knee to the helmet early in the first quarter and was down on the field for several minutes, but the veteran pass rusher was able to jog off the field and into the blue medical tent. Cameron Thomas and Yasir Abdullah should both see more defensive snaps for as long as Smith is on the sidelines being evaluated by medical staff.

headline: Smith (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
story: Smith was working through a shoulder issue this past week and drew the questionable tag for Week 1, but he was trending in the right direction after fully participating in Friday's practice. The veteran edge rusher has been given the green light to play Sunday, and he should see a healthy workload given the absences of both Jalon Walker (knee) and James Pearce (suspension).

headline: Smith (shoulder), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Steelers, is expected to play, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Unless he experiences a setback leading up to the 1 p.m. ET kickoff, Smith looks set to play through the shoulder issue that kept him from practicing Thursday and limited his participation Wednesday. With Jalon Walker (knee) out for the season and James Pearce suspended for the first eight games of the campaign, the Falcons will be counting on the 34-year-old Smith to serve as a key pass rusher.

headline: Smith (shoulder) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Steelers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Smith is dealing with a shoulder injury but was able to practice in full Friday, and he has a chance of suiting up in Week 1. However, if Smith can't play, the Falcons will need to lean on depth during Sunday's contest, and Cameron Thomas and Jared Ivey would likely see an increased snap share opposite Samson Ebukam.

headline: Daniels (neck) is questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Daniels suffered a scary neck injury in Week 6 against the Bears, when he was stretchered off the field and transported to a local hospital. He was cleared to practice in Week 7 prep and ended up finishing with a FP-LP-FP log. Daniels is understandably not in the clear just yet, but he could be given the green light by medical staff once he goes through pregame warmups Sunday.

headline: Daniels (neck) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Daniels spent a night in the hospital after being carted off the field in the third quarter of the Falcons' Week 6 loss to the Bears. The linebacker has improved greatly since the collision and is already back to full participation in practice. If Daniels can continue to string full practices together, he should have no problem suiting up for Sunday's game against the 49ers.

headline: The Falcons announced after Sunday's 31-23 loss to the Bears that Daniels (neck) was alert and had movement in all his extremities after being carted off the field in the third quarter and transported to Grady Memorial Hospital.
story: The rookie linebacker will likely remain in the hospital overnight to receive further evaluation after exiting Sunday's game following a helmet-to-knee collision with the Bears' Colston Loveland. Daniels has recorded 29 tackles, a sack and a pass breakup through Atlanta's first six contests.

headline: Daniels won't return to Sunday's game against Chicago after being carted off the field in the third quarter due to a neck injury, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: After Daniels appeared to lay motionless for a few moments following a helmet-to-knee collision with the Bears' Colston Loveland, medical staff cut off the rookie linebacker's jersey and pads before transporting him off the field with a neck brace in place. Daniels recorded seven tackles prior to his departure.

headline: Daniels (Achilles) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Monday's game against the Saints, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Daniels popped up on Friday's injury report as a limited practice participant due to an Achilles issue, but he shed an injury designation for Week 4 after logging a full practice Saturday. The rookie fourth-rounder has 10 tackles (six solo) through the first three games of the regular season.

headline: Henderson (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Henderson didn't play against the Bears in Week 6 due to a groin injury, and he was limited in the first two practices of Week 7 prep before logging a full session Friday. The full practice is a positive sign that the seventh-year defensive back will be available for Sunday's game, but his official status might not be known until about 90 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, which is when the Falcons announce their list of inactive players.

headline: Henderson (groin) was a limited participant at the Falcons' practice Wednesday, Daniel Flick of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
story: Henderson was unable to practice at all last week before ultimately missing the team's Week 6 loss to the Bears while nursing a groin injury he suffered in Week 5 versus Baltimore. The cornerback's return to practice is a step in the right direction, and he will have two more chances to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with the 49ers.

headline: Henderson (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bears, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Henderson was held out of practice all week due to a groin injury that he sustained during the Falcons' Week 5 overtime loss to the Ravens. In his absence, Avieon Terrell is expected to start opposite Mike Hughes at outside cornerback, with Mike Ford providing depth. Harrison's next opportunity to play is Week 7 against San Francisco on Sunday, Oct. 25.

headline: Henderson (groin) did not practice Wednesday, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Henderson exited Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss to the Ravens due to a groin injury. He didn't practice Wednesday. However, head coach Kevin Stefanski hasn't ruled out the 28-year-old for the Week 6 meeting with the Bears. If Henderson can't get on the field versus Chicago, Avieon Terrell would presumably see more snaps alongside Mike Hughes.

headline: Henderson (groin) is questionable to return to Sunday night's contest against the Ravens, Josh Kendall of The Athletic reports.
story: Henderson is dealing with an apparent groin injury, and his chances to return to the field before the end of Sunday's contest appear to be slim. In his absence, Avieon Terrell, Billy Bowman and Sydney Brown all stand to see an increase in opportunities in the secondary.

headline: Henderson recorded 10 tackles (nine solo), a pass defensed, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery during Monday's 45-24 win at New Orleans.
story: On a first down in Saints territory late in the first quarter, Henderson was able to rip the football right out of the hands of running back Kendre Miller in heavy traffic, setting up a touchdown to put the Falcons ahead 14-0. He may be one of the few cornerbacks meriting IDP consideration in many formats going into a Week 5 tilt versus the Ravens.

headline: Henderson is expected to step into a starting role at cornerback in Week 3, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official website reports.
story: Henderson has compiled five solo tackles and two passes defensed while playing 66 snaps on defense and 16 snaps with the special-teams unit over Atlanta's first two games of the season. The cornerback will now take over a starting role in the secondary after A.J. Terrell (groin) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday.

headline: Deablo (forearm) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo was held out of practice all week due to a forearm injury that he picked up in a Week 6 loss to Chicago. Harold Perkins and Josh Woods figure to be the top candidates to start alongside Kendal Daniels (neck) at inside linebacker in the absence of Deablo, whose next chance to play is Week 8 against Tampa Bay on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Deablo (arm) did not participate at the Falcons' practice Wednesday, Daniel Flick of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
story: Deablo suffered an arm injury in the first half of the team's 31-23 loss to the Bears in Week 6, and he was ultimately unable to return to action before the conclusion of the contest. The linebacker will have two more chances to return to practice before Sunday's contest against San Francisco.

headline: Deablo (arm) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Bears, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo exited the first half of Sunday's contest with an arm injury. The injury is severe enough to rule out the linebacker for the remainder of the contest, meaning the Falcons will need to turn to Harold Perkins at inside linebacker against this Bears offense.

headline: Deablo (arm) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Bears, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo exited the first half of Sunday's contest with an arm injury. While the starter is absent, Harold Perkins is set to fill in at inside linebacker next to Kendal Daniels.

headline: Deablo (hamstring) was a full participant at practice Thursday, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo was limited by a lingering hamstring injury at Wednesday's practice, but it appears he's now finally back up to full speed. He's on the fringe of IDP consideration in some formats going into Sunday's matchup versus the Bears.

headline: Deablo (hamstring) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo was able to play through his hamstring injury in Sunday's game versus the Ravens, but it still appears to be bothering him as Atlanta begins its preparations for Week 6. With that said, barring any setbacks, it still seems at this point that he's on track to play come Sunday versus the Bears.

headline: Deablo (hamstring) is active for Sunday night's game against the Ravens, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo was a limited participant in Friday's practice and was listed as questionable for Sunday night's game. The inside linebacker overcame his hamstring issue in time and is all set to suit up for Sunday Night Football next to fellow inside linebacker Kendal Daniels.

headline: Deablo (hamstring) is listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the Ravens, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site  reports.
story: Deablo was a limited participant in Friday's practice with a hamstring injury. The linebacker played through the injury during the Falcons' blowout win over the Saints on Monday Night Football. Diablo played 81 percent of the Falcons' defensive snaps in the contest and will likely suit up for a similar snap share in Sunday's game against the Ravens.

headline: Deablo (hamstring) is active for Monday night's game against the Saints, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo was limited throughout the Falcons' Week 4 prep and was listed as questionable ahead of Monday's contest, but his availability has now been confirmed. If Deablo were to suffer an in-game setback, Harold Perkins would be the next man up at linebacker for Atlanta.

headline: Deablo (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Saints, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: A hamstring injury limited Deablo's practice participation all week, so the sixth-year pro will have the questionable tag heading into Monday's NFC South showdown. Rookie sixth-rounder Harold Perkins would likely start next to Kendal Daniels at inside linebacker if Deablo is not cleared to play against New Orleans.

headline: Deablo (illness) is active for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: Deablo drew the questionable tag for Sunday's NFC South tilt after working through an illness during Week 2 prep, but the fifth-year pro has been given the green light to play against Carolina. He played every single defensive snap during the Falcons' 20-13 loss to the Steelers in Week 1, when he logged seven tackles (three solo) and one fumble recovery.

headline: Deablo was added to the Falcons' injury report and is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Panthers due to an illness, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: The 28-year-old linebacker may have felt under the weather upon waking up Sunday, and his availability now looks like it could come down to a game-time decision leading up to Sunday's 1 p.m. ET kickoff. In the Falcons' Week 1 loss to the Steelers, Deablo played every defensive snap and finished with seven stops and one fumble recovery.

headline: Zaccheaus (shoulder) is questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Zaccheaus' practice reps were limited during Week 7 prep due to a shoulder issue, which he may have picked up during the Falcons' Week 6 loss to the Bears. If he cannot play Sunday, then rookie third-rounder Zachariah Branch would be in line for more work both on offense and on special teams as a returner, with running back Brian Robinson also in the mix for return duties.

headline: Zaccheaus (shoulder) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: It's the second straight limited practice to begin the week for Zaccheaus, who is dealing with a shoulder injury. He may need to upgrade to full participation Friday to avoid being tagged with a designation heading into the weekend. Zaccheaus had four catches on six targets through three weeks but hasn't caught any of his five targets over Atlanta's past three contests.

headline: Zaccheaus (shoulder) was a limited participant at the Falcons' practice Wednesday, Daniel Flick of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
story: Zaccheaus appears to have picked up a shoulder injury during the team's 31-23 loss to the Bears in Week 6. The fact that he was able to practice in any capacity Wednesday would suggest that it is a minor issue, but the wide receiver will have two more chances to prove his health before Sunday's matchup with the 49ers.

headline: Zaccheaus failed to haul in his lone target during the Falcons' 45-24 win over the Saints on Monday.
story: The Falcons relied more heavily on the running game Monday, with Michael Penix attempting only 20 passes while Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson combined for 203 yards and five touchdowns on 33 carries. That left few targets to go around for the Falcons' pass catchers, with none other than Drake London (six) seeing more than three targets from quarterback Michael Penix. Zaccheaus' 21 offensive snaps were third-most among Falcons wide receivers behind London (51) and Jahan Dotson (36). However, despite entering the season as the team's WR3, Zaccheaus has just four catches (on seven targets) for 17 yards through the first four games of the regular season, and rookie wideout Zachariah Branch has seemingly taken over as Atlanta's primary returner on kickoffs and special teams. Up next for the Falcons is a Week 5 home showdown against the Ravens.

headline: Zaccheaus brought in both of his targets for nine yards and returned one punt for four yards during the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
story: Both of Zaccheaus' catches occurred in the second quarter on the same drive, which ended with a 44-yard field goal by Nick Folk. Zaccheaus is up to four catches (on six targets) for 17 yards through three regular-season games while operating as a depth option in the passing game, though Thursday's win may have been the start for a more explosive offense for the Falcons with Michael Penix under center, rather than Tua Tagovailoa, Cooper Rush (coach's decision) or Jack Strand (coach's decision). The Falcons will travel to New Orleans to face the Saints on Monday, Oct. 5.

headline: Zaccheaus caught one of three targets for three yards while returning four kickoffs for 79 yards in Sunday's 34-3 loss to the Panthers.
story: Zaccheaus played 30 offensive snaps and seven special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The veteran wideout's versatility is valued, although he remains down the depth chart for the time being.

headline: Zaccheaus caught his sole target for five yards and returned one kickoff for 29 yards in the Falcons' 20-13 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
story: Zaccheaus was the Falcons' WR3, QB3, and RB3 in Sunday's contest while also serving the No. 2 kickoff and punt returner. However, Zaccheaus played on just 18 of Atlanta's 60 offensive snaps and added another five on special teams.

headline: Zaccheaus will serve as the Falcons' WR3, the backup returner on punts and kickoffs, and the emergency third option at both quarterback and running back for Sunday's regular-season opener against the Steelers, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
story: The Falcons have two quarterbacks (Cooper Rush and Jack Strand) and two running backs (Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson) on the game-day roster for Sunday's regular-season opener. Most of Zaccheaus' playing time figures to come on three-wideout sets as he works behind Drake London and Jahan Dotson, with rookie third-rounder Zachariah Branch also in the mix for offensive snaps.

headline: Robinson (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Robinson made a surprise appearance on the Falcons' first Week 7 practice report Wednesday as limited due to a hamstring injury, but he capped the week with back-to-back DNPs and thus will miss his first game of the season Sunday. Atlanta will need to bring up Khalil Herbert from the practice squad Saturday to provide support behind top RB Bijan Robinson this weekend.

headline: Robinson (hamstring) didn't practice Thursday, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
story: After Robinson opened the week as limited Wednesday due to a hamstring injury, his downgrade to no activity one day later is cause for concern. Friday's practice and his ensuing activity level likely will determine if he's in any danger of missing Sunday's game against the 49ers. The Falcons have Khalil Herbert and Jam Miller on the practice squad in the event Robinson isn't able to handle his typical RB duties behind Bijan Robinson in Week 7.

headline: Robinson (hamstring) was a limited participant during Wednesday's practice, Daniel Flick of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
story: Robinson may have tweaked his hamstring during the Falcons' Week 6 loss to the Bears, when he recorded season lows in offensive snaps (10) and carries (two). His ability to practice in a limited capacity suggests that the injury isn't considered a serious one, and he'll have two more opportunities to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers, who he played for in 2025. In the event that Robinson cannot play, the Falcons could turn to practice squad options like Jam Miller and Khalil Herbert to serve as depth options out of the backfield behind Bijan Robinson.

headline: Robinson rushed once for one yard while reeling in both of his targets for nine yards during Sunday's 31-23 loss to the Bears.
story: Robinson registered his fewest touches in a game this season, but his two catches did match his season high from Week 2 versus Carolina. Robinson has now compiled 211 yards and four touchdowns on 42 carries while catching five of six targets for 30 yards over six contests this season. The running back is purely a top-notch safety blanket for fantasy managers who have Bijan Robinson on their roster.

headline: Robinson handled seven carries for 16 yards and did not catch his only target during Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss versus the Ravens. He also returned two kickoffs for 61 return yards.
story: Robinson's seven carries in Week 5 were the fewest he's been given in any game so far this season, and the longest of those rushes only went for four yards. Atlanta's offense still runs through Bijan Robinson, but his backup could still be a desperate, touchdown-dependent flex play in deeper formats in a Week 6 matchup versus the Bears.

headline: Robinson rushed 14 times for 62 yards and three touchdowns and brought in his sole target for five yards in the Falcons' 45-24 win over the Saints on Monday night.
story: After Bijan Robinson staked the Falcons to an early 14-0 lead with his pair of touchdown runs, it was Brian Robinson's turn from the second quarter on. The veteran backup took center stage with touchdown runs of four, eight and 11 yards in each of the last three quarters, and given the increasingly lopsided nature of the game, Brian was able to finish with just five fewer rush attempts than Bijan. Brian has now logged double-digit carries in three straight games while recording at least 50 rush yards in each of those contests, affording him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 5 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday night.

headline: Robinson rushed 10 times for 50 yards and a touchdown and returned two kickoffs for 54 yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
story: Robinson's backfield mate Bijan Robinson and No. 1 receiver Drake London stole the show Thursday while accruing 194 yards apiece, but Brian had his own moment in the spotlight when he capped off a 10-play, 92-yard drive in the third quarter with a seven-yard touchdown run. Brian Robinson now has back-to-back games with double-digit carries and has at least 50 rushing yards in each, keeping him somewhat relevant in very deep formats heading into a Week 4 road matchup against the Saints on Monday, Oct. 5.

headline: Robinson (ankle) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Listed as a limited participant for Atlanta's walk-through session Monday, Robinson was able to take every rep during Tuesday's session to clear up any concern about his availability heading into Thursday's game at Green Bay. While working in a backup role behind Bijan Robinson for the Falcons' first two games, Brian Robinson has carried 20 times for 82 yards and has recorded two receptions for 16 yards.

headline: Robinson was listed as a limited participant in Monday's walkthrough practice due to an ankle injury, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
story: The ankle issue is a new concern for Robinson, who has thus far parlayed 22 touches for 98 total yards through the first two games of the season while operating in a backup role behind Bijan Robinson. Brian Robinson will have two more chances to potentially upgrade to full practice activity, which would clear the way for him to play Thursday at Green Bay.

headline: Robinson rushed 11 times for 51 yards in Sunday's 34-3 loss to the Panthers. He added two catches for 16 yards on two targets.
story: Eight of Robinson's 13 touches came in the fourth quarter with the Falcons trailing by 31 points. It's evident he's the running back to stash behind Bijan Robinson, but Brian doesn't offer much standalone value in this anemic Atlanta offense.

headline: Robinson rushed nine times for 31 yards in the Falcons' 20-13 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
story: As expected, Robinson spelled Bijan Robinson and was a non-factor in the passing game, as Bijan out-carried him 21 to nine and out-targeted Brian 10 to zero. Brian has no standalone fantasy value but is a preferred bench stash as the next man up in the Atlanta backfield.

headline: The Athletic's Josh Kendall expects Robinson to have a goal-line role for the Falcons this season.
story: "He has shown a physical style in practice that cements his role as the new Tyler Allgeier," Kendall wrote. "Bijan Robinson fantasy managers may not like how many goal-line carries he gets." Allgeier, of course, was a thorn in the side of Bijan's fantasy investors last season, out-carrying Atlanta's lead back 19 to 17 inside the 10-yard line while matching him with seven carries apiece inside the five-yard line. Allgeier also punched in four of those seven carries for touchdowns, while Bijan scored on just two of his chances. At 6-foot-1 and 225 pounds, the team's newest Robinson profiles similarly to Allgeier as a short-yardage, between-the-tackles type who can pick up tough yards. It sounds like the former Commander and 49er going to have some sort of role in those situations for the Falcons this season, which could mute Bijan's touchdown upside.

headline: Robinson rushed five times for 14 yards and a touchdown, caught his only target for nine yards and lost a fumble in Friday's 17-12 preseason win over the Dolphins.
story: Robinson played the first quarter with most of Atlanta's starters as the Falcons held Bijan Robinson out of the exhibition slate. Brian Robinson, an offseason acquisition, capped the opening drive with a three-yard touchdown run but lost a fumble two drives later, matching Tua Tagovailoa's fumble on the possession in between. Come Week 1 against the Steelers, Brian is expected to work as Bijan's top backup in an all-Robinson 1-2 punch.

headline: The Falcons designated Williams (ankle) for return to practice from injured reserve Thursday, per the NFL's transaction log.
story: Per Tori McElhaney of the team's official site, Williams was a limited participant at practice Thursday. The transaction opens a 21-day window during which Atlanta can take Williams off IR, after which he'd be required to stay there for the remainder of the campaign.

headline: The Falcons placed Williams (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday, Will McFadden of the team's official site reports.
story: Williams was ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Steelers due to his ankle injury. The offensive tackle will evidently need more time to recover and now must miss at least four games before he is eligible to return from IR. Jake Matthews will likely get the start at left tackle in Williams' absence.

headline: Williams (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Steelers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Williams did not practice this week due to an ankle injury. It is unclear how long the reserve offensive lineman will miss due to the injury, but his absence should not impact the Falcons' starting offense much, barring injuries.

headline: The Falcons signed Dexter to a four-year, $78 million contract extension Wednesday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Atlanta acquired Dexter via a trade with the Bears back in August, and now the team will have him under contract through the 2030 season. Through three games in 2026, he has recorded seven tackles (two solo) including 0.5 sacks, and a pass defensed.

headline: Dexter (hamstring) participated at practice Tuesday, Daniel Flick of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
story: Dexter was missing practice with the Bears due to a hamstring issue prior to being traded to the Falcons on Sunday, but he now appears to be back in football shape. He projects to eventually play a significant role on Atlanta's defensive line in 2026, but it could take him a couple games to get acclimated to his new surroundings.

headline: Dexter (hamstring) was traded to the Falcons from the Bears on Sunday, NFL Insider's Jordan Schultz reports.
story: Despite drawing interest from a few teams, Dexter will head to Atlanta in exchange for Clark Phillips and a fifth-round pick. The 25-year-old Dexter has appeared in 49 regular-season games for the Bears throughout his career, totaling 115 tackles and 13.5 sacks. Dexter has been battling a hamstring injury suffered during a recent practice, so his Week 1 status is in limbo.

headline: Dexter (hamstring) is unavailable for Saturday's preseason matchup with the Titans, Brad Biggs of the Chicago Tribune reports.
story: Amid trade rumors as he enters the last year of his rookie contract, Dexter suffered a hamstring injury at practice two days ago. With the severity of the injury unclear for the moment, Dexter is unlikely to be traded and his status for Week 1 is also up in the air. The 2023 second-round pick recorded 43 tackles (21 solo), including 6.0 sacks, and two fumble recoveries during the 2025 regular season.

headline: Head coach Kevin Stefanski said Wednesday that Dalton is in a "ramp-up period" and will be inactive for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Dalton was cut by the Eagles on Oct. 9, but it didn't take long for the veteran quarterback to find work with another team, as he signed with the Falcons on Monday. He's tracking toward being available for Week 8 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Nov. 1, and Dalton could supplant Tua Tagovailoa for Atlanta's backup role behind Michael Penix.

headline: Dalton agreed to a one-year contract with the Falcons on Monday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Per Schefter, Atlanta plans to release Cooper Rush to make room on the 53-man roster for Dalton, who will likely slot ahead of undrafted rookie Jack Strand but behind Michael Penix and Tua Tagovailoa on the depth chart at quarterback. While he was with the Eagles earlier this season, Dalton beat out Tanner McKee for the No. 2 job coming out of the preseason. However, he had dropped to third on the depth chart and was ultimately cut after throwing a red-zone interception in his lone pass attempt with the Eagles while briefly filing in for starter Jalen Hurts in a Week 3 loss to the Bears.

headline: The Eagles released Dalton on Friday, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: The move comes after Dalton was demoted to QB3 duties last Sunday against the Rams. The veteran opened the season as Jalen Hurts' backup but entered Week 3 against the Bears for four offensive snaps and tossed a back-breaking interception in the end zone on his lone pass attempt. Tanner McKee will serve as Philadelphia's QB2 moving forward.

headline: Dalton is expected to serve as the Eagles' No. 3 quarterback for Sunday's game against the Rams, while Tanner McKee moves up to second on the depth chart as the top backup to Jalen Hurts, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Dalton had been active ahead of McKee as the No. 2 quarterback for each of the Eagles' first three games of the season, but he didn't see any action until midway through the second quarter of Monday's 27-7 loss to the Bears, when Hurts exited to get checked for a concussion. After three consecutive handoffs to Saquon Barkley got the Eagles to two-yard line to set up a third-and-goal, Dalton proceeded to throw a back-breaking interception in the end zone on his lone pass attempt before Hurts returned for the ensuing possession. The costly pick looks to have been enough to cost Dalton the No. 2 job, at least for one week.

headline: Dalton is active as the Eagles' top backup quarterback for Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: After facing competition from Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton for the No. 2 job behind Jalen Hurts throughout training camp and the preseason, Dalton has emerged as the victor in the job battle. Dalton will suit up for the second week in a row, while McKee is inactive as the emergency No. 3 quarterback and Payton is also donning street clothes.

headline: Dalton completed 12 of 19 passes for 104 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions in the Eagles' 30-13 preseason loss to the Bengals on Friday.
story: Dalton took over for Tanner McKee to open the second half and got plenty of work, with the highlight of his night being a five-yard touchdown pass to Carson Steele late in the third quarter. Dalton finished the preseason having completed 18 of 35 passes for 168 yards with Friday's touchdown, and his performance against the Bengals may have been sufficient to garner him the No. 2 job to open the season.

headline: Ebukam (hamstring) is active for Monday night's game against the Saints, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Ebukam missed the Falcons' Week 3 win over the Packers due to a hamstring injury he suffered in the team's Week 2 loss to the Panthers. The outside linebacker is now ready to suit up for Monday's contest alongside Divine Deablo, cementing the first and second levels of the Falcons' defense heading into a primetime matchup.

headline: Ebukam (hamstring) is officially listed as out for Thursday's game against the Packers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Ebukam was not able to practice during the week, and he'll now have to miss at least one game as he recovers from the hamstring injury he suffered during Atlanta's loss versus the Panthers in Week 2. In his absence, Jared Ivey figures to see increased reps on the edge.

headline: Ebukam (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Ebukam suffered a hamstring injury in the first half of Sunday's contest that will end his day. The outside linebacker finishes with two tackles, including 0.5 sacks. Jared Ivey and Cameron Thomas are set to share Ebukam's workload for the remainder of the game.

headline: Ebukam (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Panthers, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Ebukam suffered a hamstring injury in the first half of Sunday's contest. The starting outside linebacker logged two tackles, including 0.5 sacks, before exiting the game.

headline: The Falcons signed Snowden off the Commanders' practice squad to the active roster Tuesday, Josh Kendall of The Athletic reports.
story: Snowden has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026, but he'll get a fresh start in Atlanta and provide depth to the edge rusher position. He appeared in 15 regular-season games for the Raiders in 2025 and finished with 28 tackles (17 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and two pass defenses (including one interception).

headline: The Commanders signed Snowden (undisclosed) to the practice squad Tuesday.
story: Snowden was reinstated by the NFL on Tuesday after serving a three-game suspension, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports. The linebacker was immediately signed by the Commanders and is expected to be elevated for Sunday's game against the Colts in London. Snowden played 15 regular-season games with the Raiders in 2025, logging 28 tackles (17 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and two passes defensed, including one interception.

headline: Folk made his sole PAT in the Falcons' 31-23 loss to the Bears on Sunday.
story: Folk attempted no field goals and kicked just one PAT in the loss. The kicker is still 9-for-12 on field-goal attempts and remains a perfect 13-for-13 on PATs through six regular-season contests in 2026. This was his first game all season without a field-goal attempt.

headline: Folk converted all five of his kicks (three field goals, two extra points) during Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss to the Ravens.
story: All three of Folk's field goals came in the second half, including a 48-yarder late in the fourth quarter to give the Falcons a 23-15 lead. His three made field goals were his most of the season, and after missing three kicks in each of his first two games, Folk has made all six of his field-goal tries over his last three outings. The Falcons will stay home for Week 6 against the Bears on Oct. 18.

headline: Folk made his lone field-goal attempt all six PATs in Monday night's 45-24 win over the Saints.
story: The Falcons dominated this game from start to finish and ran the ball down New Orleans' throat, especially in the red zone, which kept Folk kicking extra points. His field goal was good from 29 yards, and the 41-year-old has made just six of nine field-goal tries and all 10 PATs through four games. All three of his misses this season are from 40-plus yards.

headline: Folk hit both field-goal attempts and all three extra-point tries in Thursday's 35-14 win over the Packers.
story: The kicker did his job during the blowout win, with his longest field goal connecting from 44 yards out. Folk missed three field goals across Atlanta's first two games, both losses, but he bounced back Thursday night. If the Falcons can keep scoring, he is a viable fantasy option.

headline: Folk made one of his two field-goal attempts in Sunday's 34-3 loss to the Panthers.
story: Folk missed a 53-yard field goal in the fourth quarter of Sunday's contest. The kicker's 41-yard attempt near the end of the first half was the Falcons' only points on the afternoon. Folk is now 3-for-6 on field-goal attempts and has made his sole PAT over the first two weeks of the season.

headline: Folk went 2-for-4 on field-goal attempts and hit his only extra-point try in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Steelers.
story: The kicker did connect from 43 and 51 yards, respectively, but he also missed from 45 and 54. Folk missed only one field-goal try in each of the last three regular seasons.

headline: Branch caught both of his targets for nine yards while adding 85 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 31-23 loss to Chicago.
story: Branch has now caught exactly two passes in three straight games, but he has only compiled 34 total yards on those receptions. The wide receiver is merely a depth option behind the likes of Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus, and he's much more valuable as a return specialist for Atlanta. On the season, Branch has reeled in nine of 10 targets for 55 yards over six contests so far.

headline: Branch caught both of his targets for 10 yards while also adding 65 kickoff-return yards and 25 yards as a punt returner during Monday night's 45-24 win over the Saints.
story: Branch garnered exactly two targets for the third game in a row as he played 13 snaps on offense. The wide receiver is primarily a special-teams asset, making him an unappealing fantasy option. As long as Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus are available, Branch has little to no offensive upside.

headline: Branch caught one pass on two targets for seven yards while logging an 18-yard punt return and a 22-yard kickoff return during the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday.
story: The rookie third-rounder has contributed on both special teams as a returner and on offense as a rotational pass catcher. He's up to three catches (on four targets) for 21 yards and 110 return yards through three regular-season games. His involvement on offense hasn't been as high as other rookie wide receivers, but the Falcons appear committed to using Branch in multiple ways to utilize his speed and explosiveness.

headline: Branch caught both of his targets for 14 yards and returned one punt for seven yards in Sunday's 34-3 loss against the Panthers.
story: Branch saw 14 offensive snaps and 11 special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver had a better Week 2 performance after not showing up in the box score for the Falcons' Week 1 loss to the Steelers. Branch remains the No. 1 punt returner for the team as well as a depth option at wide receiver.

headline: Branch returned three punts for 33 yards and one kickoff for 30 yards in the Falcons' 20-13 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
story: Branch saw 18 offensive snaps in the contest but did not show up in the box score. The wide receiver's six special-teams snaps resulted in four return attempts, hinting at a potentially expanded role with the unit in the coming weeks.

headline: Branch (hamstring) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest at Pittsburgh, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Branch opened Week 1 prep with back-to-back limited sessions due to a hamstring injury, but a full session Friday has him in the clear to make his pro debut this weekend. It's unclear what kind of role can be expected of the rookie third-round pick on offense as he jostles for snaps behind position mates Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus, but Branch at least should get on the field as a punt returner.

headline: Branch (hamstring) remained limited at practice Thursday, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Branch has been a limited participant in consecutive practices to kick off Week 1 prep, but the rookie third-round pick still has a chance to avoid an injury designation if he can upgrade to full practice participation Friday as he looks to make his NFL debut Sunday against the Steelers. Branch is expected to fill a reserve role at wide receiver to begin his career, but he's penciled in as Atlanta's primary punt returner.

headline: Branch (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Daniel Flick of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
story: It's a new injury for the rookie wideout, but a limited start to the week gives Branch a chance to suit up Sunday against the Steelers. He's competing with the likes of Olamide Zaccheaus and Jahan Dotson for offensive snaps behind Drake London.

headline: Branch returned a punt for 18 yards during the Falcons' 17-12 preseason win over the Dolphins on Friday.
story: Branch didn't see much action Friday, playing a total of four snaps (three on offense, one on special teams). However, his lone snap on special teams came as a punt returner, and he figures to see plenty of work as a returner in the upcoming season, especially if he doesn't get much playing time on offense behind Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus.

headline: Strand (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against the Packers.
story: Strand saw some action in relief of Cooper Rush in the 34-3 loss to Carolina in Week 2. However, he didn't play well, throwing for 59 yards and one interception off 8-for-15 passing, adding two carries for 16 yards. With Michael Penix (knee) and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) back in the mix, and Rush serving as the emergency signal-caller, Strand's services won't be needed in Week 3.

headline: Strand completed just eight of 15 passes for 59 yards and an interception in the Falcons' 34-3 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
story: Cooper Rush was benched after going 10-for-17 passing with no touchdowns and two interceptions. Strand came on in relief and was just as ineffective. The 22-year-old is an undrafted rookie who played his college football at tiny Minnesota State-Moorhead, so it's no surprise he wasn't ready for the NFL in his first regular-season game action. With Michael Penix (knee) potentially back for Thursday night's game at Green Bay, Strand will be a cut candidate. Strand would make more sense on the practice squad where he can learn in a no-stress environment.

headline: Strand is listed as the No. 2 quarterback for Sunday's game versus the Panthers, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
story: With Michael Penix (knee) out and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) doubtful, Cooper Rush (back) will start again in Week 2. While Strand is currently penciled in as the No. 2 signal-caller against Carolina, he'll see action if Rush is forced to miss any time.

headline: Strand could be an option for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
story: The Falcons' injury woes at quarterback could lead to Strand being active and available again in Week 2. Not only are Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) and Michael Penix (knee) dealing with injuries, but Cooper Rush is also getting treatment for his back. Tagovailoa was not practicing Wednesday, while Rush was expected to be a full participant. Penix was throwing off to the side. Depending how the injury reports shake out over the coming days, Strand could be the backup yet again for the Falcons as they host the Panthers.

headline: Strand will serve as the Falcons' backup quarterback behind Cooper Rush for Sunday's game against the Steelers, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
story: The Falcons chose to carry four quarterbacks on the 53-man roster, and that looks to have been a savvy move after Tua Tagovailoa was ruled out for Week 1 due to an oblique injury he sustained in Thursday's practice. With Michael Penix (knee) also sidelined, the Falcons will turn to the veteran Rush to start under center while Strand -- an undrafted rookie out of Minnesota State-Moorhead -- operates as the QB2. Strand played in all three of the Falcons' preseason games, completing 24 of 36 passes for 306 yards, one touchdown and one interception while turning 17 carries into 29 yards and two scores.

headline: Strand is one of four quarterbacks who made Atlanta's 53-man roster, Will McFadden of the team's official site reports.
story: The three QBs to make the roster along with Strand are Tua Tagovailoa, Michael Penix Jr. (knee) and Cooper Rush. Strand is listed as last on the team's initial depth chart, so he's unlikely to see much action, if any, barring injuries to multiple signal-callers ahead of him. Falcons GM Ian Cunningham called the team's decision to carry four quarterbacks "a little bit of an insurance policy," per the Associated Press, in acknowledgement of Tagovailoa's injury history and the knee issue Penix is still working his way back from. Still, Strand -- who signed with Atlanta as an undrafted free agent in May -- could ultimately end up on the practice squad when/if the team needs to provide more depth at other positions.

headline: Jackson (hamstring) had a tryout with the Falcons on Tuesday, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
story: The Commanders cut ties with Jackson at the beginning of September. He had been dealing with a hamstring injury, and while it's unknown if the issue is behind him, he's at least seemingly moving in a positive direction. The 2022 No. 61 overall pick appeared in 26 regular-season games for San Francisco and Washington throughout his career, garnering 24 total tackles, six sacks and one interception.

headline: Washington released Jackson (hamstring) from IR with an injury settlement Thursday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: Jackson suffered a hamstring injury during the preseason and landed on injured reserve Aug. 25. Because he has worked out an injury settlement with the Commanders, he's eligible to sign with another club and play once healthy in 2026. Jackson logged 6.0 regular-season sacks across 23 contests over his first two years in the league with San Francisco, but he's played in just three regular-season games since 2023.

headline: Penix completed 19 of 33 passes for 225 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions while rushing once for one yard in the Falcons' 31-23 loss to the Bears on Sunday. He also threw two two-point conversion passes.
story: Penix and the Falcons faced a 28-7 deficit going into the fourth quarter, but he helped bring Atlanta back with 10- and five-yard scoring tosses to Kyle Pitts and subsequent two-point conversion passes to Zachariah Branch and Drake London, respectively. Penix also connected with Jahan Dotson for a 13-yard scoring strike in the later portion of the second quarter, and Sunday's game served as Penix's first multi-TD-pass effort of the season. The third-year signal-caller also visited the medical tent in the first quarter for an undisclosed issue, but Penix appears to be healthy heading into a Week 7 home showdown against the 49ers on Sunday.

headline: Penix (undisclosed) reentered Sunday's game versus the Bears, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Penix paid a visit to the sideline tent in the first quarter of Week 6 action, but after a spell on the bench he was able to check back into the contest. If Penix eventually does miss any snaps, Tua Tagovailoa is on hand to direct the Falcons offense.

headline: Penix (undisclosed) went to the medical tent during Sunday's game against the Bears, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Penix was cleared to play in Week 6 after injuring his ribs near the end of a Week 5 overtime loss to the Ravens. The current health concern isn't known, but Tua Tagovailoa started warming up to replace Penix.

headline: Penix (ribs) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game against the Bears, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Thus, the rib injury that Penix suffered late in the fourth quarter of last Sunday's overtime loss to the Ravens is behind him. Through his three appearances this season, he's completed 52 of 77 passes (67.5 percent) for 719 yards, three touchdowns and one interception.

headline: Penix (ribs) practiced without limitations again Thursday, Daniel Flick of the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
story: Penix has faced no limitations in Atlanta's first two practices ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears, suggesting that he's good to go after subbing out late in this past Sunday's overtime loss to the Ravens, in which Tua Tagovailoa threw the game-losing interception in OT. The Falcons have scored 34.3 points per game in Penix's three starts after averaging 8.0 PPG in the first two games of the season while Penix was wrapping up the rehab on his torn ACL.

headline: Penix (ribs) was a full practice participant Wednesday, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Penix suffered a rib injury late in the fourth quarter of this past Sunday's loss to the Ravens, which didn't allow him to take the field for the Falcons' only possession of overtime. Head coach Kevin Stefanski told Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com that Penix was slated to be limited at Wednesday's practice, but afterward the quarterback himself relayed to Josh Kendall of The Athletic that he "made every throw out there" and is "good to go this week." Penix's subsequent full listing indicates as much, and he'll remain Atlanta's starting quarterback for Sunday's contest against the Bears.

headline: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said that Penix (ribs) will practice Wednesday but will be limited in some fashion, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Penix was sidelined for the extra period of Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss to the Ravens due to the rib injury, which he sustained when he was sacked late in the fourth quarter. While Stefanski didn't go into any specifics regarding the extent of Penix's injury, the coach said that the 26-year-old quarterback should be on track to start this coming Sunday against the Bears "as long as everything goes accordingly" in practice this week, per Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site. Penix looks as though he'll be listed as limited on the Falcons' initial Week 6 injury report, but he'll likely be locked in for the start if he's able to practice fully Thursday and/or Friday.

headline: The Falcons have optimism that Penix's rib injury isn't overly serious and that he'll be available to play Sunday against the Bears, Jonathan Jones and Josh Kendall of The Athletic report.
story: Penix took a hard hit to his rib area late in the fourth quarter of this past Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Ravens and was unable to play in overtime. He relayed after the game that he didn't think his rib injury was a long-term concern, and the Falcons are keeping the door open for him to start in Week 6. Per Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com, head coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday that he didn't have any new information regarding the status of Penix and wouldn't get into any further specifics regarding X-rays or imaging performed on the quarterback's ribs. Stefanski added that he expects to have a better understanding of Penix's availability Wednesday, when the Falcons will hold their first practice of the week.

headline: Penix is scheduled to undergo an MRI on Monday after exiting Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss to the Ravens due to a rib injury, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Penix sustained the injury with 27 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter, when he took a hard sack from linebacker Tavius Robinson. After giving way to backup Tua Tagovailoa for one snap, Penix checked back into the contest for the next play and threw an incomplete pass on a third-and-six before the Falcons punted the ball away. Atlanta then listed Penix as questionable to return to the game, but Tagovailoa ended up directing the offense for the team's lone possession of overtime. Per Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com, Penix said that he likely would have been able to stay in the game if the Falcons had been on offense to begin overtime, but the pain in his ribs worsened during the Ravens' long touchdown drive to kick off the extra period. Penix is confident that his latest setback on the health front isn't a long-term concern, though the upcoming MRI will ultimately determine whether he has a realistic shot at playing in Week 6 against the Bears.

headline: Penix didn't return to Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss to the Ravens after sustaining a rib injury late in the fourth quarter, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.  He completed 19 of 32 passes for 240 yards and one touchdown while rushing twice for eight yards.
story: Penix was injured after taking a big hit on Atlanta's final possession of the fourth quarter. He came back into the game after missing one play and threw an incomplete pass to close out regulation before being listed as questionable to return for the extra period. He ultimately remained on the bench for overtime, with backup Tua Tagovailoa stepping in for Penix and throwing a game-ending interception on Atlanta's second offensive play of the extra session. The oft-injured Penix will try to overcome this latest setback before the Falcons host the Bears next Sunday.

headline: Penix completed 15 of 20 passes for 223 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions and rushed twice for minus-2 yards in the Falcons' 45-24 win over the Saints on Monday night.
story: Bijan Robinson helped stake the Falcons to a 14-0 lead after one quarter, so Penix immediately had some pressure off his shoulders in only his second start since returning from last year's ACL tear. However, the third-year signal-caller still looked very sharp when called upon, and he essentially left no doubt as to the outcome of the contest when he connected with Jahan Dotson for a 31-yard scoring strike with just under 10 minutes remaining in the contest. Penix spread the ball around to seven different targets overall, and he's now completed 73.3 percent of his passes heading into a Week 5 home showdown against the Ravens on Sunday night.

headline: Penix completed 18 of 25 passes for 256 yards with one touchdown and one interception while rushing twice for minus-2 yards in the Falcons' 35-14 win over the Packers on Thursday. He also threw a two-point conversion pass.
story: Playing in his first game since Week 11 of last season, Penix started off sluggishly Thursday before finding a rhythm and putting together a near-flawless performance. Penix threw his one interception four plays into the night on a pass intended for Jahan Dotson, but he went on to record only five more incompletions the rest of the way while connecting with Austin Hooper for a five-yard touchdown pass just before halftime. Penix's chemistry with Drake London also was in fine form over the last three quarters, and he hit his No. 1 target for gains of 68 and 40 yards in the fourth quarter to help close out the upset victory. Penix should only get more comfortable the further removed he is from the third ACL surgery of his playing career, and he'll look to carry over the considerable momentum from his season debut into a Week 4 road divisional showdown against the Saints on Monday, Oct. 5.

headline: The Falcons announced that Penix (knee) has been named the team's starting quarterback for Thursday's game against the Packers, Tori McElhaney of the team's official site reports.
story: Atlanta has determined that Penix is ready to make his 2026 debut, after he was held out for the first two games of the season while ramping back up from surgery last November to address a torn ACL in his left knee. Penix was cleared to resume taking part in 11-on-11 drills in late August, then avoided any setbacks while he was a full participant in practices throughout Weeks 1 and 2. With Penix back in the fold, Cooper Rush -- who started the first two games of the season -- could be inactive for Week 3 if Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) is deemed ready to handle the No. 2 role.

headline: Penix (knee), who has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers, could be cleared to start Thursday's game against the Packers in Week 3, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Penix was ruled out for Week 2 on Friday, so Cooper Rush will start for the Falcons for the second time in as many games. However, Penix has been practicing fully for two weeks, and if he feels confident that he is ready to play on his surgically-repaired left knee, he could take over as Atlanta's starter in Week 3.

headline: The Ravens placed Robinson (pectoral) on injured reserve Saturday.
story: Robinson suffered a season-ending pectoral injury during the Ravens' Week 6 loss to the Browns. The outside linebacker will spend the rest of 2026 on IR, allowing the Ravens to carry more depth on the offensive line. The team signed offensive guard Kyle Hergel from the practice squad to the active roster in a corresponding move.

headline: Head coach Jesse Minter said Friday that Robinson will be sidelined for the rest of the 2026 season due to a pectoral injury, Cordell Woodland of 105.7 The Fan Baltimore reports.
story: Robinson was held out of practice all week, indicating that he may have picked up the injury during Baltimore's Week 6 loss to the Browns. The Ravens will likely place Robinson on injured reserve in the coming days in order to open up a spot on the 53-man roster, which they may fill with another edge rusher. The 2023 fourth-rounder is in the final year of his rookie contract and will be an unrestricted free agent in the offseason. He'll end the year with 18 tackles (nine solo), including 3.5 sacks, two pass defenses and one forced fumble over six regular-season games, and in his absence, the Ravens will rely more heavily on Zion Young, Ethan Burke and Mike Green.

headline: Robinson (pectoral) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: Robinson has now sat out practice for two straight days because of a pec issue, and his availability for Week 7 is in question. Unless he's able to practice in some capacity Friday, it's unlikely he'll play Sunday versus the Bengals.

headline: With Lamar Jackson (ankle) being downgraded to out, Huntley will be the Ravens' starting quarterback against the Bengals on Sunday.
story: Jackson initially drew the questionable tag after being limited in practice all week, but he has not recovered enough from a high-ankle sprain to make his return for Sunday's AFC North showdown.
